quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Present Simple (I feel... / I write...) & Emotions
quick_ref.Key Pattern: "I feel excited. I write on the paper."
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 8 Tier 1 words (jar, paper, write, read, smile, feel, excited, tired)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Emotional Literacy & Expression
content: Problem: Students know basic objects but cannot articulate their emotions or describe regular actions related to emotional well-being.

Solution: Week 4 introduces the "Happy Jar" concept. Students learn to express states of being ("I feel excited/tired") and associate them with positive actions ("I write", "I smile", "I read"). This creates a safe space for emotional expression while practicing the Present Simple tense.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: Pull-out oral tasks (teacher does these with 1–2 students while class works):
S1 pull-out: Show a piece of paper and a jar. Ask: "What do you write?" Student: "I write on the paper."
S2 pull-out: Ask "How do you feel?" Student: "I feel excited."
S3 pull-out: Student reads S3 VC script aloud → teacher notes pronunciation errors → recasts.
Materials needed: Print 2 copies of Card A and 2 copies of Card B.
Give Card A to Student A, Card B to Student B.
Students do not show their cards. They ask each other the target question to fill in the missing information.
Students produce complete sentences together to verify answers.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "The Happy Jar"
content: Every hero has a Happy Jar! What is inside?
Max is funny. He likes telling jokes. He likes playing games. Playing makes him happy!
Luna is friendly. She likes reading books. She likes drawing pictures. Drawing makes her happy!
Tom is brave. He likes climbing trees. He likes running fast. Running makes him happy!
What about you? What is in YOUR Happy Jar?

T / F: Max writes on the paper.
What does Max do with the paper?
Fill-in from text: I put the paper in the _______________.
Stage 3B — Inference: Why does Max smile?

content: Every hero has a Happy Jar! What is inside?
Max is funny. He likes telling jokes. He likes playing games. Playing makes him happy!
Luna is friendly. She likes reading books. She likes drawing pictures. Drawing makes her happy!
Tom is brave. He likes climbing trees. He likes running fast. Running makes him happy!
What about you? What is in YOUR Happy Jar?
Hello! I am Luna. I have a special jar.
When I play with my friends, I feel (cảm thấy) excited (hào hứng). I smile (mỉm cười) very big! I write it on my paper.
When I run fast, I feel tired (mệt mỏi). I read my happy paper.
Reading my paper makes me smile.
My jar is full of good memories.
Reading my paper makes me smile.

How does Luna feel when she plays?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Reading the Jar"
content: Every hero has a Happy Jar! What is inside?
Max is funny. He likes telling jokes. He likes playing games. Playing makes him happy!
Luna is friendly. She likes reading books. She likes drawing pictures. Drawing makes her happy!
Tom is brave. He likes climbing trees. He likes running fast. Running makes him happy!
What about you? What is in YOUR Happy Jar?
Look at my beautiful glass jar. It is full of small paper.
Every morning, I write (viết) happy things. I write about my family.
When I feel (cảm thấy) tired (mệt mỏi) or sad, I open the jar.
I read (đọc) the paper. I read about my friends.
It makes me feel very excited (hào hứng). I smile (mỉm cười)!
The happy jar is a wonderful idea. I love my happy jar!
T / F: The jar is full of small paper.
T / F: The happy jar makes him feel sad.
When does he open the jar?
Fill-in from text: It makes me feel very _______________.
Stage 3B — Inference: Why is the happy jar a wonderful idea?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Luna's Feelings"
content: Every hero has a Happy Jar! What is inside?
Max is funny. He likes telling jokes. He likes playing games. Playing makes him happy!
Luna is friendly. She likes reading books. She likes drawing pictures. Drawing makes her happy!
Tom is brave. He likes climbing trees. He likes running fast. Running makes him happy!
What about you? What is in YOUR Happy Jar?
Hello! I am Luna. I have a special jar.
When I play with my friends, I feel (cảm thấy) excited (hào hứng). I smile (mỉm cười) very big! I write it on my paper.
When I run fast, I feel tired (mệt mỏi). I read my happy paper.
Reading my paper makes me smile.
My jar is full of good memories.
Reading my paper makes me smile.
T / F: Luna has a special jar.
T / F: Luna feels tired when she plays with friends.
How does Luna feel when she plays?

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W4: jar, paper, write, read, smile
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (jar, paper, write, read, smile) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Simple (I feel... / I write...) & Emotions
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Simple (I feel... / I write...) & Emotions.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "My World — My Happy Jar"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "My World — My Happy Jar".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (jar, paper, write, read, smile usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.
